record.paper_title: Open Problems in Computability Theory and Descriptive Set Theory
record.original_question: For countable graphs G on ω, consider the property that G is isomorphic to its complement G^c. Is the set {G ∈ 2^{ω×ω} : G is a graph on ω and G ≅ G^c} Borel?

evidence.quote: Problem 32. Is the set {G ∈ 2ω×ω : G is a graph on ω and G ∼= Gc} Borel? ... The problem was solved during the workshop. Theorem 33 ... The set {G ∈ 2ω×ω : G is a graph on ω and G ∼= Gc} is Σ1_1-complete.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Identify a graph on the natural numbers ω with its edge set, viewed as an element of the Cantor space 2^{ω×ω} (with the product topology), where G ⊆ ω×ω is required to be symmetric and irreflexive. For such a graph G, let G^c denote its complement, i.e. the graph on ω whose edge set is {(i,j) ∈ ω×ω : i ≠ j and (i,j) ∉ G}. Write G ≅ G^c to mean that there exists a bijection π : ω → ω such that for all i,j ∈ ω, (i,j) ∈ G if and only if (π(i),π(j)) ∈ G^c. Consider the set
   S = { G ∈ 2^{ω×ω} : G is a graph on ω and G ≅ G^c }.
Determine the descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of S. In particular, is S a Borel subset of 2^{ω×ω}?
artifact.status_search_result: According to the workshop record where this question was posed, the problem was resolved during the workshop: the set of self-complementary countable graphs (coded in 2^{ω×ω}) is Σ¹₁-complete, and therefore not Borel.
